Answer:
answer:
The following parts of the contract are related to "Revenue/Profit Sharing" and should be reviewed by a lawyer:

From Context [1] and [4] (TUNIUCORP_03_06_2014-EX-10-COOPERATION AGREEMENT):

- Article 4.1: "Party B shall have the right to charge, on a quarterly basis, the service fee ("Service Fee") from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services, or designate another person to charge Service Fee from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. The total sum of Service Fee shall be equal to the amount of profits gained by Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. Party B shall have the right to adjust the amount of Service Fee at its own discretion, without the prior consent of Party A or its subsidiaries."

- Article 4.2: "The Service Fee of the last quarter shall be paid prior to the seventh business day following the commencement of the next quarter. Such Service Fee shall be paid to the bank account designated by Party B in writing. If Party B intends to change its bank account, it shall send a written notice to Party A seven business days in advance."

- Article 4.3: "Except as otherwise agreed hereunder, if Party A or its subsidiaries fail to pay the Service Fee in full on schedule according to provisions of Article 4.1 and Article 4.2, then Party A or its subsidiaries shall, in addition to the continuance of the payment of Service Fee in full, it shall pay Party B the liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.03% in respect of the outstanding Service Fee."

Summary:
Yes, Party A (and its subsidiaries) is required to share profits (as a Service Fee equal to the amount of profits gained) with Party B for the technology, goods, or services provided by Party B. Party B also has the right to adjust the Service Fee at its own discretion. These provisions should be carefully reviewed by a lawyer due to their significant impact on revenue/profit sharing and the unilateral adjustment right.

answer:

  - 19.3.2: "Employ or seek to employ any person who is then employed by us or any other Goosehead Business franchisee or developer, or otherwise directly or indirectly induce such person to leave his or her employment."
  - 19.3.3: "Own, maintain, develop, operate, engage in, franchise or license, make loans to, lease real or personal property to, be associated with, accept any compensation or remuneration from, and/or have any whatsoever interest in, or render services or give advice to, any Competitive Business."

- "(iii) Either directly or indirectly for him/herself or on behalf of, or in conjunction with any person, persons, partnership, corporation, or entity, own, maintain, operate, engage in, be employed by or accept any compensation or remuneration from, or have any interest in any Competitive Business."

Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Cap On Liability" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does the contract include a cap on liability upon the breach of a party’s obligation? This includes time limitation for the counterparty to bring claims or maximum amount for recovery.

Answer:
answer:
Based on the provided context, the following parts of the contract relate to "Cap On Liability" and should be reviewed by a lawyer:

From [3] (TRICITYBANKSHARESCORP_05_15_1998-EX-10-OUTSOURCING AGREEMENT):

- Section 13.4 Limitation of Liability:  
  "Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement, M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event. No lawsuit or other action may be brought by either party hereto, or on any claim or controversy based upon or arising in any way out of this Agreement be brought, after one (1) year from the date on which the cause of action arose; provided, however, the foregoing limitation shall not apply to the collection of any amounts due under this Agreement."

This section includes both a monetary cap on liability (limited to payments made in the three months prior to the event) and a time limitation for bringing claims (one year from the date the cause of action arose).

From [1] (DRIVENDELIVERIES,INC_05_22_2020-EX-10.4-CONSULTING AGREEMENT):

- Limitation of Liability:  
  "IN NO EVENT SHALL COMPANY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE AMOUNTS PAID BY COMPANY TO CONSULTANT UNDER THIS AGREEMENT FOR THE SERVICES, DELIVERABLES OR INVENTION GIVING RISE TO SUCH LIABILITY."

This section sets a cap on the maximum amount for recovery, limiting it to the amounts paid by the company to the consultant for the relevant services, deliverables, or invention.

From [2] (AIRSPANNETWORKSINC_04_11_2000-EX-10.5-Distributor Agreement):

- Section 16.2:  
  "...the liability of the Airspan Parties, taken as a whole, for each event or series of connected events arising out of or in connection with this Agreement...shall in no circumstance exceed the total amount payable by Distributor to Airspan under this Agreement for the provision of the Equipment or Software which gave rise to the loss or damage or in connection with which the loss or damage was incurred."

- Section 16.3:  
  "Airspan Parties, taken as a whole, shall be liable for physical damage to Distributor's property resulting from Airspan's negligence under or in connection with this Agreement up to a maximum aggregate amount of one million US Dollars (US$1,000,000). And Distributor, taken as a whole, shall be liable for physical damage to Airspan's property resulting from Distributor's negligence under or in connection with this Agreement up to a maximum aggregate amount of one million US Dollars (US$1,000,000)."

These sections set monetary caps on liability for both general and specific types of damages.

From [5] (GOOSEHEADINSURANCE,INC_04_02_2018-EX-10.6-Franchise Agreement):

- Reference to Section 27:  
  "...including but not limited to the waiver of punitive damages, waiver of jury trial, agreement to bring claims within one year, and agreement not to engage in class or common actions..."

This indicates a time limitation for bringing claims (one year) and a waiver of certain types of damages.

A lawyer should review all the above-highlighted sections for their implications regarding caps on liability, time limitations for claims, and any waivers of damages.

Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Cap On Liability" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does the contract include a cap on liability upon the breach of a party’s obligation? This includes time limitation for the counterparty to bring claims or maximum amount for recovery.

Answer:
answer:
The following parts of the contract are related to "Cap On Liability" and should be reviewed by a lawyer:

From [3] (TRICITYBANKSHARESCORP_05_15_1998-EX-10-OUTSOURCING AGREEMENT):

- Section 13.4 Limitation of Liability: "Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement, M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event. No lawsuit or other action may be brought by either party hereto, or on any claim or controversy based upon or arising in any way out of this Agreement be brought, after one (1) year from the date on which the cause of action arose; provided, however, the foregoing limitation shall not apply to the collection of any amounts due under this Agreement."

This section includes both a monetary cap on liability (limited to payments made in the three months prior to the event) and a time limitation for bringing claims (one year from the date the cause of action arose).

From [1] (DRIVENDELIVERIES,INC_05_22_2020-EX-10.4-CONSULTING AGREEMENT):

- Limitation of Liability: "IN NO EVENT SHALL COMPANY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE AMOUNTS PAID BY COMPANY TO CONSULTANT UNDER THIS AGREEMENT FOR THE SERVICES, DELIVERABLES OR INVENTION GIVING RISE TO SUCH LIABILITY."

This section sets a cap on the maximum amount for recovery, limited to the amounts paid under the agreement for the relevant services, deliverables, or invention.

From [2] (AIRSPANNETWORKSINC_04_11_2000-EX-10.5-Distributor Agreement):

- Section 16.2: "...the liability of the Airspan Parties, taken as a whole, for each event or series of connected events arising out of or in connection with this Agreement...shall in no circumstance exceed the total amount payable by Distributor to Airspan under this Agreement for the provision of the Equipment or Software which gave rise to the loss or damage or in connection with which the loss or damage was incurred."
- Section 16.3: "Airspan Parties, taken as a whole, shall be liable for physical damage to Distributor's property resulting from Airspan's negligence under or in connection with this Agreement up to a maximum aggregate amount of one million US Dollars (US$1,000,000). And Distributor, taken as a whole, shall be liable for physical damage to Airspan's property resulting from Distributor's negligence under or in connection with this Agreement up to a maximum aggregate amount of one million US Dollars (US$1,000,000)."

These sections set monetary caps on liability for certain types of damages.

Summary:
- [1], [2], and [3] all contain provisions that cap liability either by monetary amount or by time limitation for bringing claims. These sections should be reviewed by a lawyer to assess their adequacy and enforceability.

- The contract specifies a "minimum royalty" for each License Year, with payment schedules detailed for the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th License Years.

However, the contract does not explicitly state a "minimum order size" or a "minimum amount or units per-time period" that must be purchased. The minimum commitment is framed in terms of minimum royalty payments, not minimum purchase quantities.

A lawyer should review:
- The minimum royalty payment obligations and schedules.
- The provision regarding excess royalties offsetting minimum royalty obligations.
- Any implications these minimum royalty commitments may have on actual purchase or sales requirements.

There is no explicit minimum order size or minimum units per period required to be purchased under the contract, based on the provided excerpts. The minimum commitment is financial (royalty-based), not quantity-based.

Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Revenue/Profit Sharing" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Is one party required to share revenue or profit with the counterparty for any technology, goods, or services?

Answer:
answer:
The following parts of the contract are related to "Revenue/Profit Sharing" and should be reviewed by a lawyer:

From Context [1] and [4] (TUNIUCORP_03_06_2014-EX-10-COOPERATION AGREEMENT):

- Article 4.1: "Party B shall have the right to charge, on a quarterly basis, the service fee ("Service Fee") from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services, or designate another person to charge Service Fee from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. The total sum of Service Fee shall be equal to the amount of profits gained by Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. Party B shall have the right to adjust the amount of Service Fee at its own discretion, without the prior consent of Party A or its subsidiaries."

- Article 4.2: "The Service Fee of the last quarter shall be paid prior to the seventh business day following the commencement of the next quarter. Such Service Fee shall be paid to the bank account designated by Party B in writing. If Party B intends to change its bank account, it shall send a written notice to Party A seven business days in advance."

- Article 4.3: "Except as otherwise agreed hereunder, if Party A or its subsidiaries fail to pay the Service Fee in full on schedule according to provisions of Article 4.1 and Article 4.2, then Party A or its subsidiaries shall, in addition to the continuance of the payment of Service Fee in full, it shall pay Party B the liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.03% in respect of the outstanding Service Fee."

Summary:
Yes, Party A (and its subsidiaries) is required to share profits (as a Service Fee equal to the amount of profits gained) with Party B for the technology, goods, or services provided by Party B. Party B also has the right to adjust the Service Fee at its own discretion. These provisions should be carefully reviewed by a lawyer due to their significant impact on revenue/profit sharing and the unilateral adjustment right.

Answer:
answer:
Relevant parts of the contract related to "Audit Rights" that should be reviewed by a lawyer include:

From Passage [1] (CYBERIANOUTPOSTINC_07_09_1998-EX-10.13-PROMOTION AGREEMENT):

9.5 Audit Rights. Each party will have the right to engage an independent third party to audit the books and records of the other party relevant to the calculation of Retail Impressions or CNET Sales, upon reasonable notice and during normal business hours, and the other party will provide reasonable cooperation in connection with any such audit. The party requesting the audit will pay all expenses of the auditor unless the audit reveals an underpayment by the other party of more than 5%, in which case the other party will reimburse all reasonable expenses of the auditor.

This section gives each party the right to audit the books and records of the counterparty relevant to specific calculations under the agreement, with conditions regarding notice, cooperation, and allocation of audit costs.

There is no mention in this passage of the right to audit physical locations—only books and records.

Summary:

- The section should be reviewed by a lawyer for scope, process, and cost allocation of audit rights.
